newsitem.title: USA: Boston's Hotel Meridien sold for $100 mln - report.
newsitem.headline: Boston's Hotel Meridien sold for $100 mln - report.

text.p: Boston's Hotel Meridien has been sold to an investment group representing Hong Kong's Lo family for about $100 million or $290,000 per room, the Boston Business Journal reported on Friday.
Acording to unnamed sources, the sale of the hotel, currently owned by Beacon Cos and General Electric Investments Corp to Pacific Eagle Holdings Ltd will close in June.
The companies involved did not return phone calls from Reuters.

Local real estate analysts told the BBJ that the sale price of the Meridien is almost double the $150,000 per room paid for the Copley Plaza Hotel in 1994 and indicates the strength of the Boston market.
Occupancy rates in the Meridien average in the "high 70s" and room rates start above $220 a night, a hotel manager told the newspaper.
Pacific Eagle, which recently sold two U.S. properties to finance the Meridien purchase, will likely use the "1030 exchange" tax measure to save on taxes, sources told the BBJ.
